title: Cursor Cuts Prices, Adds Spend Controls Amid Tokenomics Reckoning
excerpt: Cursor's dramatic price cuts and new enterprise spend controls this week signal the end of the 'move fast and burn tokens' era in AI-assisted development. Companies are finally grappling with the true economic cost of AI-generated code.
post_draft:
How much is your AI coding assistant actually costing you?

Cursor just cut prices and added spend controls—and it's a wake-up call for the entire industry.

The "move fast and burn tokens" era is ending. Companies are finally doing the math on AI-generated code and realizing the bill is far steeper than they thought.

This shift matters for your security posture too. When cost becomes a constraint, teams make different choices about which code gets AI assistance, which gets reviewed, and what actually ships to production.

The tokenomics reckoning is here, and it's forcing everyone to ask harder questions: What's AI actually worth? Where should it live in your development pipeline? And what's the real cost of moving fast?

Read the full breakdown of what Cursor's moves mean for enterprise AI adoption and your bottom line.
